subject: Request: termination-for-convenience carveout + auto-renew removal (MSA redline)
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-07-19 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: remove auto-renew & add TFC carveout (MSA redline)

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this call last week. Per our legal team, we're not able to accept the standard auto-renew language as-is and need an explicit termination-for-convenience (TFC) carveout in the MSA or an alternative off-ramp that gives Acme equivalent exit latitude.

Attached is our redline (Acme_MSA_Redline_0709.pdf) showing the requested edits:
- Remove automatic renewal clause or provide a firm opt-out window no less than 60 days prior to renewal.
- Add mutual TFC with a 30–60 day notice window (our preference is 30 days).
- If TFC is limited, add a capped termination fee for early exit.

We're still committed to the deployment but procurement needs the contract mechanics clarified before they can sign. Can your team review and propose a commercially reasonable compromise we can take back to legal? Ideally by end of next week — procurement has a July 26 budget hold deadline.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
(sarah.liu@acme-analytics.com)

[Attachment: Acme_MSA_Redline_0709.pdf]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding Acme's redline and ask. Key asks from Acme: remove/modify auto-renew and add TFC or termination fee. Procurement timeline: July 26 budget hold.

Quick thoughts:
- Sales: we want to avoid a wholesale removal of auto-renew since revenue predictability suffers; can we offer an opt-out window + commercial minimum term?
- Legal (Mina): need your recommended language we can present to Acme. If we can offer mutual TFC with a reasonable notice and a capped termination fee for the first X months, we keep most of the protections.
- Ops (Karthik): confirm whether a 30/60/90 day notice affects onboarding timelines or billing cutoff.

Action: Mina, can you draft one-page options (prefer/acceptable/last resort) and attach a redline we can share back to Acme by COB 7/22? If not possible, flag the commercial/credit implications.

Thanks,

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: remove auto-renew & add TFC carveout (MSA redline)

Hannah / team —

Reviewed Acme's redline. We can accommodate a compromise without exposing Redwood to material churn risk if we structure it carefully. Proposed options (summarized):

Option A (preferred): Mutual TFC with 60-day notice + 6-month minimum service period post-activation. Auto-renew remains, but Customer may opt-out by providing notice at least 60 days before renewal. No termination fee after 6 months.

Option B (sales-favorable): Mutual TFC with 30-day notice but with an early termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed MRR if termination occurs within first 6 months. Auto-renew opt-out window = 60 days.

Option C (last resort): Remove auto-renew; replace with fixed term equal to initial committed period and explicit non-renewal unless both parties agree — this is a heavier lift commercially.

Attached is a tracked redline (MSA_Redline_Suggested_v3.pdf) that implements Option A and calls out the billing/mechanics. Key legal notes: 
- Make the TFC mutual (protects Redwood if we must offboard capacity).
- Clarify billing proration and settlement timeline (30 days after notice), and define how pre-paid credits are handled.
- Keep an escape for operational impact (if on-prem or private deployment, extend notice to 90 days).

Recommend we present Option A to Acme and indicate Option B as a fallback. If Acme insists on 30-day TFC with no fee, we should request a one-time onboarding credit or minimum spend guarantee.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_Redline_Suggested_v3.pdf]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: remove auto-renew & add TFC carveout (MSA redline)

Sarah —

Thanks for the redline. We reviewed internally and want to propose a pragmatic middle path so procurement can proceed while protecting both parties. Summary of our proposal (attached OrderForm_Amendment_07022.docx):

- Mutual termination-for-convenience (TFC) with 60 days' written notice.
- 6-month minimum service period from activation date; if Customer terminates within the first 6 months, a capped termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed fees applies. No termination fee after 6 months.
- Auto-renew remains in the MSA, but Customer will have an opt-out window of no less than 60 days prior to the renewal effective date.
- If deployment is Private or on-prem, notice increases to 90 days to account for deprovisioning.

If that structure is acceptable, we can push the redline to DocuSign and preserve the current commercial terms. We need confirmation by COB 2026-07-23 to keep the quoted pricing and the July onboarding window.

Appreciate your flexibility — attaching the proposed amendment and a tracked MSA excerpt.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0148

[Attachment: OrderForm_Amendment_07022.docx]
[Attachment: MSA_Redline_Suggested_v3.pdf]
